caption:
🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Wednesday, 11 November 2026

1. ⚖️ High Court rules Home Office unlawfully treated Eritrean as an adult
The High Court held that a series of Home Office decisions to treat a young Eritrean asylum seeker as an adult, so he could be removed to France under the UK-France treaty, were unlawful.

2. 🏥 Social care review says governments have been 'asleep at the wheel'
Baroness Louise Casey has warned that the sector is 'fundamentally fragmented'.

3. 👴 Tories would have to raise state pension age above 70, minister claims
Treasury minister Torsten Bell has claimed Kemi Badenoch's Conservatives would have to raise the state pension age above 70 to meet the cost of keeping the triple lock.

4. 🎓 Regulator says universities should return to exams as AI hits coursework
The Office for Students, England's higher education regulator, says universities should go back to traditional exams and in-person presentations.

5. 📉 Nvidia's value falls by about $430bn in two days after CEO admits affair
Nvidia's market value has fallen by about $430bn (£322bn) in two days after its CEO, Jensen Huang, admitted to an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.

6. ♿ Disabled people in England wait up to two years for wheelchairs, report says
A report by Paula Sussex, the parliamentary and health service ombudsman for England, says delays involving NHS bodies and private firms that make wheelchairs have profound consequences and limit users' ability to lead independent lives.

7. 🚨 US soldier suspected of spying for Russia is arrested by UK counter-terror police
The man faces 'serious' espionage allegations relating to Russia.

8. 👑 Kate opens up about her recovery from cancer in rare interview
The Princess of Wales says that nature is her 'sanctuary'.

Sources: Free Movement, The Independent, Guardian, Sky News. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay. Photos: Daniel Torok/White House / Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

items.title: High Court rules Home Office unlawfully treated Eritrean as an adult
items.body: The High Court held that a series of Home Office decisions to treat a young Eritrean asylum seeker as an adult, so he could be removed to France under the UK-France treaty, were unlawful. The case is R (EXR) v Secretary of State for the Home Department (No.3).

items.title: Social care review says governments have been 'asleep at the wheel'
items.body: Baroness Louise Casey has warned that the sector is 'fundamentally fragmented'. The review says governments have been 'asleep at the wheel' for decades.

items.title: Tories would have to raise state pension age above 70, minister claims
items.body: Treasury minister Torsten Bell has claimed Kemi Badenoch's Conservatives would have to raise the state pension age above 70 to meet the cost of keeping the triple lock. Labour has announced reforms to the triple lock to come into force in the next parliament.

items.title: Regulator says universities should return to exams as AI hits coursework
items.body: The Office for Students, England's higher education regulator, says universities should go back to traditional exams and in-person presentations. Lecturers complained that AI has made it 'close to impossible' to assess coursework.

items.title: Nvidia's value falls by about $430bn in two days after CEO admits affair
items.body: Nvidia's market value has fallen by about $430bn (£322bn) in two days after its CEO, Jensen Huang, admitted to an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The chief executive is being urged to quit.

items.title: Disabled people in England wait up to two years for wheelchairs, report says
items.body: A report by Paula Sussex, the parliamentary and health service ombudsman for England, says delays involving NHS bodies and private firms that make wheelchairs have profound consequences and limit users' ability to lead independent lives.

items.title: US soldier suspected of spying for Russia is arrested by UK counter-terror police
items.body: The man faces 'serious' espionage allegations relating to Russia. He was detained following an investigation involving the FBI.

items.title: Kate opens up about her recovery from cancer in rare interview
items.body: The Princess of Wales says that nature is her 'sanctuary'. In a rare interview, she speaks about her recovery from cancer and says: 'We are not alone.'
